_comment: Hand-written exhibition reference data, merged with data/collection.json at render time. Design, designer and edge-inscription facts follow the Royal Mint's published design list. Keys under 'designs' match the design name in a coin's variant field; a 'Design|Year' key overrides the plain design key when the same design was re-cut by a different artist.

series.name: The Round Pound
series.subtitle: United Kingdom, 1983–2015
series.lede: Thirty-four years of British coinage on a single denomination — a new reverse almost every year, cycling through the four nations.
intro: The round pound replaced the £1 note in April 1983 and ran for thirty-four years. The Royal Mint treated its reverse as a rolling canvas — a new design almost every year, cycling through the four nations.
It is one of the few modern coins a collector completes by design rather than by date. Each is shown beside the artist who cut it, the nation it stands for, and the motto milled on its edge.
series.closing: The round pound was demonetised in October 2017, replaced by the twelve-sided bimetallic pound. Coins of that new type are held in this collection but are not part of this exhibition.

2nd portrait.label: Second portrait
2nd portrait.note: The Queen wearing the ‘Girls of Great Britain and Ireland’ tiara.

3rd portrait.label: Third portrait
3rd portrait.note: A crowned portrait in the George IV State Diadem, signed RDM.

4th portrait.label: Fourth portrait
4th portrait.note: A closer, unidealised profile signed IRB.

5th portrait.label: Fifth portrait
5th portrait.note: The final circulating portrait of Elizabeth II, signed JC.

edges.DECUS ET TUTAMEN: ‘An ornament and a safeguard’ — a motto for milled edges, which were cut to make clipping detectable.
edges.NEMO ME IMPUNE LACESSIT: ‘No one provokes me with impunity’ — the motto of the Order of the Thistle, for Scotland.
edges.PLEIDIOL WYF I'M GWLAD: ‘True am I to my country’ — from the Welsh national anthem.
edges.DOMINE DIRIGE NOS: ‘Lord, guide us’ — the motto of the City of London.
edges.PRO TANTO QUID RETRIBUAMUS: ‘What shall we give in return for so much’ — the motto of Belfast.
edges.NISI DOMINUS FRUSTRA: ‘Without the Lord, all is in vain’ — the motto of Edinburgh.
edges.Y DDRAIG GOCH DDYRY CYCHWYN: ‘The red dragon will show the way’ — the motto of Cardiff.
edges.Decorative pattern: The bridge series carried a decorative milled pattern in place of a motto.

Royal Arms.note: The full achievement of the Royal Arms — the design that opened the series in 1983 and was brought back in 1993, 1998 and 2003. The 1998 striking never entered circulation: it was issued only in collector sets, which makes it the scarcest date of the whole series.

Royal Arms|2015.note: Not a reissue of Sewell's arms but a new design: Noad raises the lion and unicorn and works the four national flowers into the field. It was the last design struck on a round pound.

Scottish Thistle.note: A thistle encircled by the royal diadem, from Durbin's floral set for the four nations.

Welsh Leek.note: A leek within the royal diadem.

Northern Irish Flax.note: The flax plant, Northern Ireland's emblem, within the royal diadem.

English Oak.note: An oak tree within the royal diadem, closing Durbin's four-nation cycle.

Crowned Royal Shield.note: A one-year type: the shield of the Royal Arms beneath a crown, struck only in 1988.

Scottish Lion.note: The lion rampant within a double tressure, from Sillman's heraldic set.

Celtic Cross.note: A Celtic cross with a pimpernel flower and a torc.

English Three Lions.note: Three lions passant guardant, the arms of England.

Forth Bridge.note: The first of four bridges. Ellis engraved each as a piece of engineering rather than heraldry.

Menai Bridge.note: Telford's suspension bridge over the Menai Strait.

Egyptian Arch Bridge.note: The Egyptian Arch railway bridge at Newry.

Gateshead Millennium Bridge.note: The tilting footbridge over the Tyne — the only modern structure in the bridge set.

Royal Shield.note: The whole shield of the Royal Arms. Dent's 2008 redesign broke that shield across the six smaller denominations, so the pound carries the complete device the others fragment.

London.note: A capital-cities badge: the arms of the City of London.

Leek and Daffodil.note: Noad's floral emblems set: the leek and daffodil of Wales, crowned.

Rose and Oak.note: The rose and oak of England, crowned.

Flax and Shamrock.note: The flax and shamrock of Northern Ireland, crowned.

Thistle and Bluebell.note: The thistle and bluebell of Scotland, crowned.
